Build a balanced, analysis-ready panel

Source: R/panel.R
ntl_panel.Rd

Turns the long output of ntl_extract() or ntl_splice() into a balanced unit x period panel. Unit-periods that were never extracted (for example because no file existed) are added with NA values instead of disappearing, and low-coverage observations can be set to NA with an explicit threshold.

Usage

ntl_panel(
  x,
  value = "ntl_sum",
  id_col = NULL,
  min_share_valid = NULL,
  transform = c("log1p", "asinh", "log", "none"),
  balance = TRUE,
  frequency = NULL
)

Arguments

x

An ntl_long data frame with a single series.

value

Column holding the outcome (default "ntl_sum").

id_col

Unit identifier column. Defaults to the one recorded by ntl_extract().

min_share_valid

If set, observations with share_valid below this threshold get NA values and low_coverage = TRUE.

transform

Transformation stored in column ntl: "log1p" (default), "asinh", "log" (zeros become NA) or "none".

balance

Complete the unit x period grid.

frequency

"month" or "year". Defaults to the frequency recorded by ntl_extract().

Value

An ntl_panel data frame with the id column, period, year, month (monthly panels), t (consecutive integer time index), the outcome, ntl (transformed outcome), ntl_missing, low_coverage and the coverage diagnostics. The columns t and the id work directly with fixest::feols(ntl ~ ... | id + t).

Examples

ex <- ntl_example()
m <- ntl_files(ex$dir, "eog_vnl_monthly")
m <- m[m$series == "eog_vnl_monthly_npp" &
         m$period < as.Date("2022-01-01"), ]
long <- ntl_extract(m, ex$units_old,
                    id_col = "district", quiet = TRUE)
p <- ntl_panel(long, min_share_valid = 0.5)
table(p$month, p$ntl_missing)
#>     
#>      FALSE TRUE
#>   1      6    0
#>   2      6    0
#>   3      6    0
#>   4      6    0
#>   5      6    0
#>   6      3    3
#>   7      3    3
#>   8      6    0
#>   9      6    0
#>   10     6    0
#>   11     6    0
#>   12     6    0
